source.title: NTK-SAP: Improving neural network pruning by aligning training dynamics
source.authors: Yite Wang; Dawei Li; Ruoyu Sun

record.file_problem: none; full paper text supplied, including appendix
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares training accuracy of pruned subnetworks across datasets and pruning methods, bearing conceptually on V1's training-error outcome. It does not test the other claim versions.
record.gate_note: Training-accuracy results are shown in Figure 9 and described as higher for NTK-SAP than for other foresight pruning methods. Exact curve values are figure-only in the supplied text; cited prior work is not recorded as this paper's result.
record.test_reason: The study develops an NTK-based pruning method and compares its subnetworks with other pruning methods. Its training-accuracy results establish relative pruning performance, without establishing V1's near-zero training-error outcome or testing the mechanisms and comparisons in V2–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that NTK-SAP is competitive across the tested datasets and models, and Appendix H reports higher subnetwork training accuracy than competing foresight pruning methods. They also acknowledge the computational cost of iterative pruning.
record.recipe_differences: The paper evaluates pruning at initialization followed by training, rather than directly testing whether sufficiently large dense networks trained from random initialization reach near-zero training error. The pruning method is data-agnostic and compares several masks.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset, model, sparsity ratio and pruning method vary in the training-accuracy results; the supplied text does not state exact figure values by condition.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix H reports higher training accuracy for NTK-SAP subnetworks than for competing foresight pruning methods; absolute values cannot be recovered from the supplied figure text.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The pruning mask chosen at initialization affects subsequent trainability, and NTK-SAP identifies easier-to-train subnetworks in the tested settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix G reports that NTK-SAP better preserves the initial dense-network NTK spectrum, while sparse and dense spectra subsequently diverge.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: NTK spectrum preservation provides a pruning criterion associated with favorable subnetwork performance.

record.problems: Training-accuracy outcomes appear only in Figure 9; exact values are not stated in the supplied text. The experiments cover pruned networks and do not establish the near-zero training-error threshold or label-corruption conditions in V1.
record.rows_left_out: No separate method-by-sparsity rows were extracted because Figure 9 provides curves without text-reported per-condition values; the three rows retain each model and dataset's reported aggregate curve coverage.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error in sufficiently large networks; corrupted or random labels; and controlled effects of model size, early stopping or regularized recipes.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious-minimum frequencies and adding student neurons.
Training-error degradation with depth and comparisons with identity shortcuts or special initialization.
Comparisons of initialization schemes, signal or gradient preservation, training speed and trainable depth.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, loss recovery, curvature trajectories and divergence.
Training speed and learning-rate tolerance with versus without BatchNorm, including Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: All methods use Kaiming normal initialization; this does not test its advantage over other initializations. BatchNorm mode differences concern pruning-score computation and do not test BatchNorm's training acceleration. Figure-axis ticks alone cannot establish training-accuracy outcomes.

versions.untested_parts: The paper tests training accuracy only for pruned models on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and Tiny-ImageNet. It does not test random or corrupted labels, zero/near-zero training error as a stated threshold, smaller unpruned models, early stopping, or the full range of recipes in the version.
